questions.question: Mahmud Gawan was granted the title of Chief of the Merchants or Malik-ut-Tujjar by __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Humayun Shah**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Title of Malik-ut-Tujjar: A Recognition of Mahmud Gawan's Influence**
 
• Humayun Shah, the Bahamani ruler, bestowed the title of "**Chief of the Merchants" or Malik-ut-Tujjar upon Mahmud Gawan**.
 
• This title was a recognition of Gawan's significant contributions to the **Bahmani Sultanate's trade and commerce**.
 
• Mahmud Gawan, a Persian merchant and scholar, rose through the ranks of the Bahmani government due to his administrative and diplomatic skills.
 
• He served as the prime minister under several Bahmani rulers, including Humayun Shah.
 
• During his tenure, Gawan implemented various reforms that enhanced the state's economic prosperity and strengthened its trade relations with other regions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The title of Malik-ut-Tujjar was not just a symbolic gesture.
 
• It reflected the importance of trade and commerce in the Bahmani Sultanate and Gawan's instrumental role in fostering economic growth.
 
• Under his leadership, the kingdom witnessed a flourishing trade network, attracting merchants from far and wide.
 
• Gawan's policies encouraged trade and commerce, leading to increased revenue for the state and improved living standards for its people.
 
• In addition to his economic contributions, Gawan was also a patron of learning and culture.
 
• He established schools and libraries, promoting education and intellectual pursuits.
 
• His legacy as a statesman, economist, and patron of the arts continues to be celebrated centuries later.

questions.question: Deimachus who was a Greek ambassador came to India during the reign of the Mauryan king, ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bindusara**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Deimachus was a Greek ambassador who came to India during the reign of the Mauryan king Bindusara.
 
• Bindusara was the second Mauryan emperor, ruling from c. 297 to c. 273 BCE.
 
• He was the son of Chandragupta Maurya, the founder of the Maurya Dynasty.
 
• Bindusara maintained diplomatic relations with various Hellenistic states, including the Seleucid Empire.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bindusara**

 
 
• Bindusara, also known as Amitraghata, was the second emperor of the Mauryan dynasty.
 
• He succeeded his father, Chandragupta Maurya, and ruled from c. 297 BCE to c. 273 BCE.
 
• Bindusara is known for his administrative skills and the expansion of the Mauryan Empire.
 
• He maintained friendly relations with the Hellenistic kingdoms, which were established by the successors of Alexander the Great.
 
 
 
• **Deimachus**
 
 
• Deimachus was a Greek envoy sent by Antiochus I, the Seleucid king, to the Mauryan court.
 
• His visit to India is recorded as part of the diplomatic relations between the Mauryan Empire and the Hellenistic world.
 
• Deimachus succeeded Megasthenes, another Greek ambassador, at the Mauryan court.
 
 
 
• **Mauryan Empire**
 
 
• The Mauryan Empire was the first large-scale empire in India, founded by Chandragupta Maurya in 322 BCE.
 
• It is known for its significant achievements in political, military, and cultural fields.
 
• The empire reached its zenith under Ashoka the Great, who is renowned for his promotion of Buddhism and non-violence.
 
 
 
• **Diplomatic Relations**
 
 
• During the Mauryan period, diplomatic relations were established with several Hellenistic kingdoms, including the Seleucid Empire.
 
• These relations were crucial for trade, cultural exchange, and political alliances.
 
• Greek ambassadors like Megasthenes and Deimachus played a key role in these diplomatic efforts.

questions.question:
Arrange the ruling dynasties of India in chronological order:

A. Gajpati Kingdom of Orissa

B. Delhi Sultanate

C. Sultanate of Ahmadnagar, Bijapur and Berar

D. Sultanate in Jaunpur, Kashmir and Madura

Ε. Sultanate of Golconda

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is - __Delhi Sultanate, Sultanate in Jaunpur, Kashmir, and Madura, Gajpati Kingdom of Orissa, Sultanate of Ahmadnagar, Bijapur, and Berar, Sultanate of Golconda__**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__ **

__
 
• **Delhi Sultanate__**

 __
 
• The Delhi Sultanate__ was established in the early 13th century (1206 CE) and lasted until 1526 CE.
 
• It was one of the earliest Islamic empires in India, ruled by dynasties like the Slave, Khilji, Tughlaq, Sayyid, and Lodi.
 
 
 
• **__Sultanate in Jaunpur, Kashmir, and Madura__**
 __
 
• The regional Sultanates__ in Jaunpur, Kashmir, and Madura emerged during the late 14th and 15th centuries.
 
• These sultanates were offshoots or successors of the Delhi Sultanate and contributed to regional governance.
 
 
 
• **__Gajpati Kingdom of Orissa__**
 __
 
• The Gajpati Kingdom__ was established in the mid-15th century (1434 CE) and ruled over present-day Odisha and neighboring regions.
 
• They were known for their patronage of Hinduism and art and architecture.
 
 
 
• **__Sultanate of Ahmadnagar, Bijapur, and Berar__**
 __
 
• These Deccan Sultanates__ emerged in the 16th century after the decline of the Bahmani Sultanate.
 
• They played a significant role in resisting Mughal expansion into the Deccan region.
 
 
 
• **__Sultanate of Golconda__**
 __
 
• The Golconda Sultanate__ was established in the mid-16th century (1518 CE) and lasted until the late 17th century.
 
• It was known for its wealth, especially from diamond trade, and its splendid architecture.
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] __Additional Information__ **

__
 
• **Delhi Sultanate's Significance__**

 __
 
• It marked the beginning of Islamic rule in India__ and introduced significant cultural and architectural changes.
 
• The sultanate faced invasions from the Mongols and challenges from regional kingdoms.
 
 
 
• **__Deccan Sultanates__**
 __
 
• These sultanates, including Ahmadnagar, Bijapur, Berar, and Golconda, were key players in the Deccan region.
 
• They are known for resisting the Mughals and fostering unique cultural and architectural styles.
 
 
 
• **Gajpati Kingdom__**
 __
 
• The Gajpati rulers were great patrons of Jagannath culture__ and constructed iconic temples in Odisha.
 
• Their rule was marked by a synthesis of regional and pan-Indian traditions.

questions.question:
In the context of the Indian national movement, which of the following statements is correct regarding the Rowlatt Act? 

I. This Act was passed in 1921.

II. This Act allowed detention of political prisoners without trial for two years.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Rowlatt Act was passed in 1919 and not in 1921, making statement I incorrect.
 
• This Act allowed the British government to detain political prisoners without trial for up to two years, thereby confirming statement II as correct.
 
• The official name of the act was the Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act of 1919.
 
• It aimed to curb revolutionary activities and anti-British sentiments by allowing the government sweeping powers of arrest and detention.
 
• The act faced strong opposition from Indian leaders like Mahatma Gandhi, who initiated protests and satyagraha against it.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Background and Protests Against the Rowlatt Act:**

 
 
• Introduced by the British government in March 1919, the act was designed to extend the wartime emergency measures into peacetime.
 
• It permitted the arrest of individuals without any warrant and their detention without trial, which led to widespread outrage.
 
• As a response, Mahatma Gandhi launched the Rowlatt Satyagraha, a nationwide nonviolent protest against the draconian law.
 
 
 
• **The Jallianwala Bagh Massacre:**
 
 
• The Rowlatt Act protests culminated in the tragic Jallianwala Bagh massacre on April 13, 1919, when General Dyer ordered open fire on a peaceful gathering in Amritsar.
 
• This incident caused hundreds of deaths and injuries, sparking widespread resentment and intensifying the national freedom struggle.
 
 
 
• **Impact on the Indian National Movement:**
 
 
• The Rowlatt Act and the subsequent massacre unified Indians across regions and classes in their opposition to British rule.
 
• It marked a turning point in the Indian national movement, leading to the rise of mass protests and civil disobedience campaigns under Gandhi's leadership.
 
 
 
• **Repeal of the Rowlatt Act:**
 
 
• Due to its unpopularity and the failure to enforce it effectively, the Rowlatt Act was eventually repealed in 1922.

questions.question:
Match the following Geographical Factors with their Descriptions:

 
 

 **Geographical Factors**
 **Descriptions**
 
 

 a. Topography
 1. Avoid extreme hot or cold climates
 
 

 b. Climate
 2. Suitable plains for farming
 
 

 c. Soil
 3. Prefer living near fresh water sources
 
 

 d. Water
 4. Areas of better housing, education
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is **a-4 b-1, c-2, d-3**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Topography**:

 
 
• Topography refers to the landscape and terrain of a region. Areas with favorable topography, like plains, are more suitable for farming and settlement because they are easy to build on and cultivate.
 
• This aspect includes mountains, valleys, plains, and plateaus, which influence human activities. For example, mountainous regions may restrict farming but can offer protection and natural resources.
 
• Human settlements tend to develop in areas where the topography facilitates agriculture, transportation, and construction.
 
 
 
• **Climate**:
 
 
• Climate involves long-term patterns of temperature, humidity, wind, and precipitation. People tend to avoid extreme climates (e.g., too hot or too cold), preferring temperate regions for comfort and health.
 
• The climate of an area affects the type of vegetation that can grow, the kind of activities people can engage in, and the overall lifestyle of the inhabitants.
 
• Moderate climates are more attractive for human habitation as they provide a more comfortable living environment.
 
 
 
• **Soil**:
 
 
• Soil quality is crucial for agriculture. Fertile soils in plains and river valleys support robust agricultural activity, influencing settlement patterns.
 
• The availability of arable soil dictates the kind of crops that can be grown and the subsequent development of agricultural based societies.
 
• Rich, fertile soil attracts settlers because it ensures a steady food supply and supports farming livelihoods.
 
 
 
• **Water**:
 
 
• Proximity to fresh water sources, such as rivers, lakes, and streams, is essential for drinking, sanitation, agriculture, and industry, making these areas prime targets for settlement.
 
• Water resources are vital for human survival, and historically, most civilizations have emerged and thrived near abundant fresh water sources.
 
• Access to water also facilitates transportation and trade, further enhancing the attractiveness of these regions for human habitation.
 
 

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Geographical factors significantly influence human settlement patterns, the type of activities they engage in, and their lifestyle.
 
• Topographical features like mountains and rivers not only shape weather patterns but also determine the ease of movement and habitation in an area.
 
• Climate dictates the type of clothing, housing, and even social customs prevalent in a region.
 
• The quality of soil impacts agricultural productivity, which in turn affects local economies and sustainability.
 
• Water availability is perhaps the most critical factor, as it is indispensable for drinking, agriculture, and industrial use, making it a central element in human settlement and development.

questions.question: Isochrone lines on a map connect places having equal:
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is:** "Travel time"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Isochrone Lines:**

 
 
• Isochrone lines on a map connect points where the travel time to a specific location is equal.
 
• These lines are used to analyze accessibility and mobility from a given point, typically considering factors such as transport modes and road conditions.
 
• Isochrone maps are widely used in urban planning, transportation studies, and geographic analysis to assess how far one can travel within a certain time frame.
 
 
 
• **(Physical distance): **
 
 
• Isochrone lines are not related to physical distance. Instead, they represent accessibility based on time, which may vary depending on transport networks and traffic conditions.
 
• For example, two locations at the same physical distance from a point may have different travel times due to differences in road quality or congestion.
 
 
 
• **(Transport cost): **
 
 
• Transport cost is not a factor in creating isochrone lines. Isochrones solely focus on travel time, regardless of cost.
 
• Cost analysis is a separate concept often studied in economic geography or transport economics.
 
 
 
• **(Road length): **
 
 
• Isochrone lines do not represent road length; they represent time taken to travel, which depends on factors like speed limits, traffic, and transport modes, not just the length of the road.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Isochrone Maps:**
 
 
• Used in urban planning to understand accessibility to essential services like hospitals, schools, and public transportation.
 
• Helpful in transportation modeling to plan routes, assess congestion, or optimize travel time.
 
• Used by businesses to determine service areas and customer accessibility within a specific time frame.
 
• Aid in emergency response planning by identifying areas that can be reached within a certain time during crises.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Isochrone Map Creation:**

 
 
• Isochrone maps are created using Geographic Information Systems (GIS) tools. These tools calculate travel time based on input data such as road networks, speed limits, and traffic conditions.
 
• They can also factor in different modes of transport, such as walking, driving, or public transit, to produce accurate representations.
 
 
 
• **Historical Use:**
 
 
• The concept of isochrone mapping dates back to the early 20th century and has evolved significantly with advancements in GIS technologies.
 
• Initially used for railway planning, the method has expanded to encompass multi-modal transport analysis.
 
 
 
• **Related Concepts:**
 
 
• **Isodistance Maps:** These maps connect points at the same physical distance from a central location, differing from isochrone maps which focus on time.
 
• **Network Analysis:** Isochrone mapping is a type of network analysis in GIS, focusing on accessibility within a given network.

questions.question: Sinhala is the official language of which among the following countries?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sri Lanka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Sinhala** is one of the official languages of Sri Lanka, alongside Tamil.
 
• It is primarily spoken by the Sinhalese ethnic group, who make up around 74% of the country's population.
 
• The Sri Lankan Constitution recognizes Sinhala as the official language under Article 18, while Tamil is also designated as a national language.
 
• Sinhala has a rich literary tradition dating back over 2,000 years and uses the **Sinhala script**, which is derived from the ancient Brahmi script.
 
• The language is an integral part of Sri Lanka's cultural and national identity, influencing its arts, traditions, and education systems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sinhala Script:** It is an abugida writing system derived from Brahmi, primarily used for Sinhala and Pali languages.
 
• **Historical Context:** Sinhala has been used as a medium for Buddhist scriptures and ancient chronicles like the "Mahavamsa," which chronicles Sri Lanka's history.
 
• **Demographics:** Tamil, the other national language of Sri Lanka, is predominantly spoken by Tamil ethnic groups and Muslims, constituting about 26% of the population.
 
• **Language Policy:** Post-independence, the Official Language Act of 1956 declared Sinhala as the sole official language, which later sparked ethnic tensions and reforms to include Tamil.
 
• **UNESCO Recognition:** Certain Sinhala literary works and manuscripts are recognized as part of world heritage for their cultural and historical significance.

questions.question: Which writ is issued by a high court or supreme court when a lower court has considered a case going beyond its jurisdiction?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Prohibition**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Prohibition** is issued by a higher court to a lower court or tribunal to prevent it from exceeding its jurisdiction or usurping a jurisdiction that it does not possess.
 
• This writ is used to control the actions of lower courts and ensure that they do not overstep their boundaries.
 
• The writ of prohibition directs inactivity, ordering the lower court or tribunal to stop the proceedings in a case that falls outside its jurisdiction.
 
• It is a form of judicial control over the lower courts by the higher courts like the High Courts and the Supreme Court in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Quo Warranto**

 
 
• This writ is issued to inquire into the legality of a claim of a person to a public office. It restrains a person from acting in a public office to which they are not entitled.
 
• The purpose is to prevent illegal usurpation of public office by an individual.
 
 
 
• **Habeas Corpus**
 
 
• This writ is issued to produce a person who has been detained, whether in prison or private custody, before a court and to release that person if such detention is found illegal.
 
• The primary objective is to ensure the personal liberty of citizens against unlawful detention.
 
 
 
• **Certiorari**
 
 
• This writ is issued by a higher court to a lower court or tribunal to transfer a case pending with the latter to itself or to quash the order of the latter in a case.
 
• It is issued on grounds of excess of jurisdiction or lack of jurisdiction or error of law apparent on the face of the record.

questions.question: In India, which act was enacted to provide for the prevention, control, and abatement of environmental pollution?

options.text: The Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act was enacted by the Government of India in 1981.
 
• The main objective of the Act is to prevent, control, and abate air pollution in India.
 
• The Act provides for the establishment of Central and State Pollution Control Boards to monitor and control air pollution.
 
• It empowers these boards to set standards for air quality and emissions, and to take measures to ensure compliance with these standards.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Environment Protection Act**

 
 
• Enacted in 1986, the Environment Protection Act provides for the protection and improvement of the environment.
 
• It allows the central government to set standards for the quality of the environment and to regulate and prohibit industrial activities that may harm the environment.
 
• The Act encompasses all forms of pollution, including air, water, and soil pollution.
 
 
 
• **The National Green Tribunal Act**
 
 
• Passed in 2010, this Act establishes the National Green Tribunal (NGT) for effective and expeditious disposal of cases relating to environmental protection and conservation of forests and other natural resources.
 
• The NGT deals with civil cases under various environmental laws in India.
 
 
 
• **The Forest Conservation Act**
 
 
• Enacted in 1980, the Forest Conservation Act aims to conserve forests and to regulate deforestation.
 
• It restricts and regulates the de-reservation of forests or use of forest land for non-forest purposes.
 
• The Act requires prior approval from the central government for any activity that leads to the diversion of forest land.

questions.question: Calculate the gravitational potential energy of a 50 kg object placed 5 meters above the ground. (Use g = 9.8 m/s²​)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **2450** J

**Calculation:**

m = 50 kg

h = 5m,

g = 9.8 m/s²

Using the formula for gravitational potential energy:

U = mgh

U = 50 × 9.8 × 5

U = 2450 J

**So, gravitational potential energy is 2450 J**

questions.question: When lead nitrate is heated, it decomposes to form lead monoxide (PbO), nitrogen dioxide (NO₃), and oxygen (O₂). The brown gas seen during the reaction is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**nitrogen dioxide (NO2)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lead nitrate** is a chemical compound with the formula Pb(NO3)2.
 
• When heated, lead nitrate undergoes **thermal decomposition** to produce lead monoxide (PbO), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), and oxygen (O2).
 
• The **chemical equation** for this reaction is: 2 Pb(NO3)2 → 2 PbO + 4 NO2 + O2.
 
• **Nitrogen dioxide (NO2)** is a **brown gas** and is responsible for the brown fumes observed during the decomposition of lead nitrate.
 
• Lead monoxide (PbO) is a yellow solid that remains after the decomposition.
 
• Oxygen (O2) is a colorless gas that is released during the reaction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nitric oxide (NO)**__

 __
 
• **Nitric oxide** is a colorless gas.
 
• It is formed by the oxidation of nitrogen during combustion processes.
 
• It is not produced during the decomposition of lead nitrate.
 
 
 
• **Lead monoxide (PbO)**__
 __
 
• **Lead monoxide** is a yellow or red solid.
 
• It is one of the products of the decomposition of lead nitrate but does not cause the brown fumes.
 
 
 
• **Oxygen (O2)**__
 
 
• **Oxygen** is a colorless and odorless gas.
 
• It is essential for respiration and combustion processes.
 
• Oxygen is released during the decomposition of lead nitrate but does not cause the brown fumes.

questions.question: On which of the following Sikh Guru's birth anniversary is the Prakash Parv celebrated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Guru Nanak Dev**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Prakash Parv** is celebrated to mark the birth anniversary of **Guru Nanak Dev**, the founder of Sikhism.
 
• Guru Nanak Dev was born on **15 April 1469**, but his birthday is celebrated annually based on the **lunar calendar (Kartik Purnima)**, which usually falls in November.
 
• The festival is observed with immense devotion and spiritual fervor in **Gurdwaras worldwide**, especially at **Golden Temple, Amritsar**.
 
• Followers participate in **Nagar Kirtan** (processions), recite **Gurbani (hymns)**, and organize **Langar** (community kitchens).
 
• Guru Nanak Dev emphasized the principles of **equality, selfless service, and devotion to God**, which are central to Sikhism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Guru Nanak Dev:**

 
 
• He was the **first of the ten Sikh Gurus** and laid the foundation of Sikhism.
 
• His teachings are compiled in the **Guru Granth Sahib**, the holy scripture of Sikhs.
 
• He traveled extensively across India and beyond, spreading his message of **unity, compassion, and devotion.**
 
 
 
• **Kartik Purnima:**
 
 
• It is a sacred day in the Hindu and Sikh calendars, marking the full moon in the Kartik month.
 
• It is celebrated as **Guru Nanak Jayanti** and also holds significance for Hindus as the day of **Dev Diwali.**
 
 
 
• **Langar:**
 
 
• A free community kitchen started by Guru Nanak Dev to promote the principle of **seva (selfless service)** and equality.
 
• Langar is open to all, irrespective of caste, religion, or gender.
 
 
 
• **Nagar Kirtan:**
 
 
• A religious procession organized during Guru Nanak Jayanti where Sikhs sing hymns and carry the holy Guru Granth Sahib.
 
• It is a way to spread the teachings of Sikhism among the masses.

questions.question: Tadoba national park known for sheltering tiger, panther and bear is located in
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chandrapur (Maharashtra)**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tadoba National Park** is a prominent national park located in the Chandrapur district of Maharashtra.
 
• The park is known for its rich biodiversity and is a crucial habitat for several endangered species, including tigers, panthers, and bears.
 
• It is part of the larger Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve, which is one of the oldest and largest national parks in Maharashtra.
 
• The park is named after the local deity "Tadoba" or "Taru," worshipped by the tribal people of the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tadoba National Park** was established in 1955 and later merged with the Andhari Wildlife Sanctuary to form the Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve.
 
• The park covers an area of approximately 625.4 square kilometers, providing a safe haven for a variety of flora and fauna.
 
• It is renowned for its dense forests, scenic landscapes, and diverse wildlife, attracting tourists and wildlife enthusiasts from around the world.
 
• The best time to visit the park is between October and June, when the weather is conducive for wildlife spotting and safari tours.
